notes: Page 1 is an introductory text page by the designer about how Brick Sketches began. It has no building step, so it adds no pieces or joins. The parts list (140 pieces) was received and will be used for the following pages.

Unrelated to this page: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorization. This session is non-interactive, so I couldn't do it. Authorize them in your claude.ai connector settings. Until then they're unavailable.

This page is a general guide on opening the box, sorting the pieces by colour and starting to build. It has no model-building step, so it adds no pieces.
Step 1 places one white 4x12 plate as the canvas base.

Step 2 lays two yellow 2x4 tiles and two yellow 2x2 wedge plates along the back two rows of the base. A wedge sits at each end, so the strip covers 2+4+4+2 = 12 studs, and each piece rests only on b1.
I read the strip as the back two rows of the plate, with the front two rows left bare.

Step 3 adds a yellow 2x2 jumper plate (b6) in the middle and four yellow 1x2 tiles (b7-b10) on the front rows of the white plate b1. Two tiles sit to the right of the jumper, and the other two flank it.
Step 4 adds two blue 2x8 plates (b11, b12), turned to run front-to-back, one on each side of the jumper. Each overhangs the front edge of the base.
I could not tell from the drawing exactly which studs the blue plates cover, so I listed only b1 as what they rest on. They may also clutch some of the earlier yellow pieces.

Page 9 listed b4 and b5 as yellow wedges and b2 and b3 as yellow tiles, as drawn. The remaining-parts list suggests the manual may use the blue 87079 and black 24307 there instead. I kept the colours as drawn.
Step 5 adds two white 4x12 plates (b13, b14) in front of the base plate b1. They sit under the overhanging parts of the blue 2x8 plates b11 and b12, so the blue plates clutch them from above.
That is why b13 and b14 have empty rests_on: nothing is beneath them. The blue plates actually rest on them, which I couldn't record on the earlier page, so I recorded it as joins.
I read the new plates as one directly in front of b1 and one in front of that, together with b1 forming a roughly square 12-stud-wide base.
Step 6 adds a red 2x10 plate down the middle, with a gray 1x8 groove tile on each side of it, and four yellow tiles along the outer edges.
Across the 12-stud width, the columns run: yellow 2, blue 2, gray 1, red 2, gray 1, blue 2, yellow 2. Two yellow tiles sit end to end on each side, so each side is 8 studs long.

I drew the yellow tiles as 2x4 tiles (lego-87079) because their proportions match the 2x4 tiles from step 2. The step 3 tiles on the previous page may also have been 2x4 tiles rather than 1x2 tiles. I can't correct that page now.
The red plate overhangs the front edge of the base.
rests_on lists are my best reading of which base plates lie under each piece.
Step 7 adds one more white 4x12 plate (b22) at the front of the base. Together with b1, b13 and b14 this makes the full 12x16 canvas.
It sits under the overhanging front end of the red 2x10 plate b15, which holds it in place. Nothing is under it, so rests_on is empty and the clutch is recorded as a join.
The gray tiles b16 and b17 may also overlap this plate. I only recorded the red plate.

Step 8 adds four yellow 2x4 tiles (b23-b26) and two yellow 1x2 tiles (b27, b28) over the front-left and front-right white studs on both sides of the red plate's front end. The result is a yellow frame around the blue, gray and red centre.
I placed two 2x4 tiles on each side and one 1x2 tile at each side of the red plate's front end. The exact split between b14 and b22 is my best reading of the drawing.

Step 9 completes the yellow border along the front edge. It adds one yellow 2x6 plate (b29), which leaves studs showing near the front-left of the canvas, and four yellow 1x2 tiles (b30-b33) on either side of it.
All five pieces are on the front white plate b22. The exact positions along the front edge, and whether any also clutch neighbouring tiles, are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 10 puts a black 2x4 plate on each back corner (b34 left, b35 right) and a red 2x2 round plate with an axle hole (b36) over the yellow jumper's centre stud at the middle back.

The back-corner positions follow the drawing. The earlier yellow 2x4 'tiles' at the back strip should have no studs, so the black plates probably clutch the wedge plate studs and the surrounding pieces. I listed the wedge and the neighbouring tile as supports, which is my best guess.
The red round plate is on the jumper b6's single stud. It may also overlap neighbouring pieces.

Step 11 puts a blue 2x4 tile (b37) on the red centre plate, with a black 2x2 plate with two studs (b38, b39) at each end of it. This covers most of the red strip and leaves some red visible at the front.
All three clutch the red 2x10 plate b15. The gray tiles beside it have no studs, so I didn't list them as supports.
The blue 2x4 tile is the blue lego-87079 from the parts list, drawn blue in this step.
Step 12 places two black 4x8 half-round plates (b40 at the back, b41 at the front). Together they form Minnie's round black head, with the blue tile showing in the gap between them.
Each half rests on its black 2x2 plate (b38 or b39) and on the blue 2x8 plates (b11, b12) underneath. They may also touch other studs; I listed the supports I could see.
Step 13 adds a black 2x4 plate (b42), a black wedge plate (b43) and two red angled heart plates (b44, b45) around the front of the head, building the lower body or outfit.
The wedge icon shows roughly 7 studs, so I read it as a 2x4 wedge plate (lego-51739) rather than the 2x2 left wedge (lego-24299).
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing. The front-edge pieces may clutch neighbouring plates as well.
Step 14 adds a second black 2x4 wedge plate (b46) at the back of the head. It mirrors the wedge b43 at the front and covers the back half of the head, b40, and the black plate b38 under it.
The supports are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 15 places a white 3x6 half-round plate with a 1x2 cutout (b47) on the black head as the start of the face. It wraps around the blue tile.

Two black 1x2 grille tiles (b48, b49) are shown dropping onto the back-left of the head. I took these to be the black 1x2 grille tiles (lego-2412b) from the parts list and placed them on the back head half b40, which is my best reading of the arrows.
Step 16 adds a black left wedge plate 2x2 (b50) and a black right wedge plate 2x2 (b51) on the black head, on either side of the white face piece. They fill in the head outline.
The remaining-parts list suggests the black right wedge was already used as b4 or b5 on page 9, where I recorded yellow wedges. I kept the colours as drawn on each page.
Which half of the head each wedge sits on, b40 or b41, is my best reading of the drawing.
Step 17 places two black 6x6 round plates with a hole as Minnie's ears, one at the back-left (b52) and one on the right (b53).
Each ear sits on its black 2x4 corner plate (b34 or b35) and overlaps the head plate b40. These supports are my best reading of the drawing.

Step 18 adds a white 2x3 plate (b54) and two white 4x4 round-corner plates (b55, b56). With the half-round plate b47 they make up the white face over the black head, leaving the blue tile showing in the middle.
I took the 1x piece to be a plain 2x3 plate (lego-3021), judging by its six studs.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 19 builds a red strip (the bow knot or dress band) between the two red heart plates at the front. It uses two red 1x1 plates, one red 1x2 jumper plate and two red 1x1 grooved tiles.
I put the red pieces on the black 2x4 plate b42 between the hearts, with the 1x1 plates at each end resting on a heart plate (b44 or b45) as well.
The order along the strip is my reading of the drawing.
Step 20 adds two red 1x1 quarter tiles (b62, b63) and four white 1x1 round tiles (b64-b67) on the two red heart plates. This makes the white polka dots and finishes the red shoes or bow.
I put one quarter tile and two white round tiles on each heart plate (b44 left, b45 right). The exact stud each piece goes on is my reading of the drawing.
Step 21 turns the model upside down. Two white 1x16 bricks (b68, b69) are added along the two long edges of the underside, clutching the bottoms of the four base plates b1, b13, b14 and b22.

A white 1x10 brick (b70) fills the 10 studs between the two rails at one end. I placed it at the end of the plate b1 because 12 - 2 = 10 studs fit exactly. The drawing doesn't make its position clear.
Because the model is flipped, rests_on here means the base plates the bricks clutch onto, not pieces below them.
Step 22 adds a white 1x10 plate (b71) between the two white 1x16 rails (b68, b69) at the end of the underside opposite the 1x10 brick b70.
I took it to clutch the front base plate b22, since I put b70 on the back plate b1. The model is still flipped, so rests_on means the base plate it clutches.

Step 23 adds two white 1x3 plates (b72, b73) and one light bluish gray 1x4 plate (b74), which together cover the 10 studs of the 1x10 plate b71. The gray plate goes in the middle and a white plate at each end.
I took all three to sit only on b71. They may also touch the rails b68 and b69, but I couldn't confirm that from the drawing.

Step 24 adds a white 3x2 rounded-end plate with a hole (b75) in the middle of the end row, and two white locking hinge plates (b76, b77) on the white 1x3 plates b72 and b73. These make the hinge mount for the stand on the underside.
The two arrows show the second hinge plate dropping onto the row next to the rounded plate. I placed one hinge plate at each end of the row.
The rounded plate's supports (b74 and b70) are my best reading of the drawing. No hinge to a mating part appears on this page, so I recorded no other_joins.
Step 25 adds a white 1x10 plate (b78) along the end wall next to the hinge row, so the hinge plates and rounded plate sit in a closed 10-stud-wide frame.
I placed it on the 1x10 brick b70. Which end of the model b70 is on is uncertain, so this is my best reading of the drawing.

Page 32 is a separate sub-assembly: a U-shaped handle. Step 1 pushes the red 2-long axle into the first white elbow tube. Step 2 joins a second elbow on the other end of that axle to make a U. Step 3 pushes a long gray axle (the labelled '11') into each free elbow end.
The parts box also shows two white hinge cylinders (lego-57360), but none of the three steps shows one being placed. I did not add them and expect them on a later page.
None of these pieces rests on another, so rests_on is empty. The axle joins are recorded in other_joins.

Step 4 pushes a white hinge cylinder (b84, b85) onto the free end of each long axle of the U-handle. The U-handle is then lowered into the underside of the model, so the hinge cylinders clip onto the two hinge plates b76 and b77 (marked '1:1' for axle length).
Which hinge cylinder pairs with which hinge plate is assumed; the handle is symmetrical, so it shouldn't matter. The handle swings on the hinges as a stand or hanger.
Step 27 puts a light bluish gray 1x1 round brick on each of the four corners of the underside rails. Two sit on the left 1x16 rail (b68) and two on the right one (b69). They act as feet or stops.
The model is still upside down, so rests_on means the rail brick each one is pressed onto. Which end of each rail gets which brick is symmetrical and doesn't matter.
Step 28 caps each of the four gray round bricks (b86-b89) with a white 2x2 round plate with rounded bottom (boat stud, b90-b93). These form the feet of the model.
Each foot is on one brick; I paired them in order.

Step 29 turns the model right side up and builds a small checkered knot (the bow). A red 2x2 round plate (b94) gets two tan 1x1 plates (b95, b96) on one diagonal and two red quarter tiles (b97, b98) on the other. The finished sub-assembly is placed on the red round plate b36 at the back of the head.
I recorded b94 as resting on b36, the red round plate from step 10, because the arrow points at that spot.
Step 30 adds the third black 4x8 half-round plate (b99). It covers the top half of the white face as Minnie's hair line, between the ears.
I listed the back wedge b46, the white half-round b47 and the white 2x3 plate b54 as what it clutches. This is my best reading of the drawing.
Step 31 adds a light bluish gray 3x4 plate with 1x4 centre studs (b100) in the middle of the face, between two white 3x3 round tiles (b101, b102) that form the eyes.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing, since the pieces overlap the black hair plate b99 and the white face pieces.

Step 32 adds a second white 3x6 half-round plate with a 1x2 cutout (b103) for the lower face, a blue 1x2 rounded plate with two open studs (b104), and a white 4x4 curved macaroni tile (b105) that curves along the front edge of the face as the smile.
I assumed the blue plate and the curved tile sit on the new white plate b103. I put the new half-round plate over b47, b54, b55 and b56. These supports are my best reading of the drawing.

Step 33 adds a white 2x3 plate (b106) on top of the gray centre plate b100 (the nose or brow), two black 1x2 tiles (b107, b108) on the ears, and two white 1x1 quarter tiles (b109, b110) on the lower-face plate.
I took the black tiles to be lego-3069b (Tile 1x2 with Groove, Black) from the parts list. I put one on each ear plate, b52 and b53.
The white quarter-tile positions are only roughly visible, so I placed them on b103 as my best guess.

Step 34 is built 2x. Each copy is a white 2x6 round-corner plate with two black half-circle 1x1 tiles that together make an oval pupil. The copies are placed side by side at the eye positions on the face.
The 2x box and the arrows show two identical copies. I listed all 6 pieces (b111-b116).
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing, since the eye plates overlap the hair plate b99, the gray plate b100 and the white 2x3 plate b106.

Step 35 adds a yellow 2x2 round plate with an axle hole (b117, the centre of the face), a light bluish gray hinge brick base (b118) and two black 2x2 curved macaroni tiles (b119, b120). The curved tiles arc around the lower face.
I identified the gray piece as the 1x2 hinge brick base (lego-3937) from its shape. It is probably the base for a hinged top plate later.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 36 is built 2x. Each copy is a red angled heart plate with two white 1x1 round tiles as polka dots. One copy goes on each ear plate, b52 (left) and b53 (right), beside the bow.
I listed all 6 pieces (b121-b126). I paired each heart with the ear plate it sits on.
Step 37 adds a red 2x2 round tile with a bottom stud holder (b127) in the middle of the bow, between the two red heart plates b121 and b122 on the ears.
I assumed it clutches studs on both hearts. It may also overlap the earlier bow sub-assembly b94 and its tiles.

Step 38 adds a white 2x6 double round-corner plate (b128) on the upper face over the two eye plates, two white 1x1 plates (b129, b130), and two white 1x1 quarter tiles (b131, b132). The tiles are shown dropping onto the new plate's corners.
The remaining-parts list suggests white quarter tiles were already used up, so the quarter tiles here may actually be red. I kept the white seen in the drawing.
Where the two 1x1 plates sit is not clear from the drawing; I put one beside each eye plate. All supports are my best guess.
Step 39 adds two black 1x2 grille tiles (b133, b134), one at the outer edge of each eye plate (b111, b112), as eyelashes.

Correction to page 15: I recorded the two black tiles b48 and b49 there as lego-2412b grille tiles. The parts list has only two grille tiles, so those were probably plain black 1x2 tiles (lego-3069b), and the grille tiles belong here. I can't change b48 and b49 on this page.

Step 40 adds a white 1x2 plate (b135) with a white 1x2 grooved tile pressed on top (b136), and two white 1x2 sloped bricks (b137, b138). Together they make a raised nose on the face, sitting on the hinge brick b118 and the 2x3 plate b106.
Exactly which studs the slopes clutch is my best reading of the drawing.

Step 41 builds Minnie's nose. A black round dome brick (b140) is pressed onto a white 1x2 hinge top plate (b139). The assembly is then clipped onto the gray hinge brick base b118 that sits in the middle of the face.

The small plate icon is not clearly labelled. By elimination from the remaining-parts list, and because it shows a hinge finger on the end, I identified it as the white thin hinge top plate (lego-3938).
The red jumper plate lego-15573 is no longer in the list; it was used earlier as b59. The nose can pivot on the hinge.
This page has no building step. It shows the finished model from the back, with the U-shaped handle swung out on its hinges as a stand.
The yellow and white 1x2 grooved tiles (lego-3069b) still show as unplaced. They may be spares, or the manual may use them on a later page.
This page has no building step. It shows the finished Minnie Mouse model standing up on its folded-out stand.
This page is an advertisement for the LEGO product feedback prize draw, with copyright text. It has no building step, so it adds no pieces.
The yellow and white 1x2 grooved tiles (lego-3069b) were never placed in any step I saw. They are probably spare pieces, though the manual may place them on a page I didn't see.
These four entries replace the earlier entries with the same ids. No new pieces were added. Only rests_on changed; type and colour are unchanged.

b34 and b35 (black 2x4 plates, page 16) no longer list the yellow tiles b2 and b3. Those tiles have no studs, so the plates can only clutch the wedge plates' studs: b34 on b4 and b35 on b5. I'm leaving the 2x4 plates overhanging the tiles.
b57 and b58 (red 1x1 plates, page 25) are one stud each, so they can rest on only one piece below. I dropped b42 and kept the heart plate each one sits on: b57 on b44 and b58 on b45.
My reading of the drawings for these four supports is still approximate. These are the changes that satisfy the stud-count checks.

These four entries must REPLACE the earlier entries with the same ids. I can only send additions, so I can't delete the old edges myself. The old edges are wrong: b34 on b2, b35 on b3, and b57/b58 on b42. Please drop them.
b34 and b35 (black 2x4 plates, page 16) rest only on the wedge plates b4 and b5. The yellow 2x4 tiles b2 and b3 have no studs, so nothing can clutch them from above.
b57 and b58 (red 1x1 plates, page 25) are one stud each, so they rest on one piece only: the heart plates b44 and b45.
No new pieces or other_joins are added. Everything else in the graph stands as given.

Step 17 places two black 6x6 round plates with a hole as Minnie's ears, one at the back-left (b52) and one on the right (b53).
Each ear sits on its black 2x4 corner plate (b34 or b35) and overlaps the head plate b40. These supports are my best reading of the drawing.

Step 18 adds a white 2x3 plate (b54) and two white 4x4 round-corner plates (b55, b56). With the half-round plate b47 they make up the white face over the black head, leaving the blue tile showing in the middle.
I took the 1x piece to be a plain 2x3 plate (lego-3021), judging by its six studs.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 19 builds a red strip (the bow knot or dress band) between the two red heart plates at the front. It uses two red 1x1 plates, one red 1x2 jumper plate and two red 1x1 grooved tiles.
I put the red pieces on the black 2x4 plate b42 between the hearts, with the 1x1 plates at each end resting on a heart plate (b44 or b45) as well.
The order along the strip is my reading of the drawing.
Step 20 adds two red 1x1 quarter tiles (b62, b63) and four white 1x1 round tiles (b64-b67) on the two red heart plates. This makes the white polka dots and finishes the red shoes or bow.
I put one quarter tile and two white round tiles on each heart plate (b44 left, b45 right). The exact stud each piece goes on is my reading of the drawing.
Step 21 turns the model upside down. Two white 1x16 bricks (b68, b69) are added along the two long edges of the underside, clutching the bottoms of the four base plates b1, b13, b14 and b22.

A white 1x10 brick (b70) fills the 10 studs between the two rails at one end. I placed it at the end of the plate b1 because 12 - 2 = 10 studs fit exactly. The drawing doesn't make its position clear.
Because the model is flipped, rests_on here means the base plates the bricks clutch onto, not pieces below them.
Step 22 adds a white 1x10 plate (b71) between the two white 1x16 rails (b68, b69) at the end of the underside opposite the 1x10 brick b70.
I took it to clutch the front base plate b22, since I put b70 on the back plate b1. The model is still flipped, so rests_on means the base plate it clutches.

Step 23 adds two white 1x3 plates (b72, b73) and one light bluish gray 1x4 plate (b74), which together cover the 10 studs of the 1x10 plate b71. The gray plate goes in the middle and a white plate at each end.
I took all three to sit only on b71. They may also touch the rails b68 and b69, but I couldn't confirm that from the drawing.

Step 24 adds a white 3x2 rounded-end plate with a hole (b75) in the middle of the end row, and two white locking hinge plates (b76, b77) on the white 1x3 plates b72 and b73. These make the hinge mount for the stand on the underside.
The two arrows show the second hinge plate dropping onto the row next to the rounded plate. I placed one hinge plate at each end of the row.
The rounded plate's supports (b74 and b70) are my best reading of the drawing. No hinge to a mating part appears on this page, so I recorded no other_joins.
Step 25 adds a white 1x10 plate (b78) along the end wall next to the hinge row, so the hinge plates and rounded plate sit in a closed 10-stud-wide frame.
I placed it on the 1x10 brick b70. Which end of the model b70 is on is uncertain, so this is my best reading of the drawing.

Page 32 is a separate sub-assembly: a U-shaped handle. Step 1 pushes the red 2-long axle into the first white elbow tube. Step 2 joins a second elbow on the other end of that axle to make a U. Step 3 pushes a long gray axle (the labelled '11') into each free elbow end.
The parts box also shows two white hinge cylinders (lego-57360), but none of the three steps shows one being placed. I did not add them and expect them on a later page.
None of these pieces rests on another, so rests_on is empty. The axle joins are recorded in other_joins.

Step 4 pushes a white hinge cylinder (b84, b85) onto the free end of each long axle of the U-handle. The U-handle is then lowered into the underside of the model, so the hinge cylinders clip onto the two hinge plates b76 and b77 (marked '1:1' for axle length).
Which hinge cylinder pairs with which hinge plate is assumed; the handle is symmetrical, so it shouldn't matter. The handle swings on the hinges as a stand or hanger.
Step 27 puts a light bluish gray 1x1 round brick on each of the four corners of the underside rails. Two sit on the left 1x16 rail (b68) and two on the right one (b69). They act as feet or stops.
The model is still upside down, so rests_on means the rail brick each one is pressed onto. Which end of each rail gets which brick is symmetrical and doesn't matter.
Step 28 caps each of the four gray round bricks (b86-b89) with a white 2x2 round plate with rounded bottom (boat stud, b90-b93). These form the feet of the model.
Each foot is on one brick; I paired them in order.

Step 29 turns the model right side up and builds a small checkered knot (the bow). A red 2x2 round plate (b94) gets two tan 1x1 plates (b95, b96) on one diagonal and two red quarter tiles (b97, b98) on the other. The finished sub-assembly is placed on the red round plate b36 at the back of the head.
I recorded b94 as resting on b36, the red round plate from step 10, because the arrow points at that spot.
Step 30 adds the third black 4x8 half-round plate (b99). It covers the top half of the white face as Minnie's hair line, between the ears.
I listed the back wedge b46, the white half-round b47 and the white 2x3 plate b54 as what it clutches. This is my best reading of the drawing.
Step 31 adds a light bluish gray 3x4 plate with 1x4 centre studs (b100) in the middle of the face, between two white 3x3 round tiles (b101, b102) that form the eyes.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing, since the pieces overlap the black hair plate b99 and the white face pieces.

Step 32 adds a second white 3x6 half-round plate with a 1x2 cutout (b103) for the lower face, a blue 1x2 rounded plate with two open studs (b104), and a white 4x4 curved macaroni tile (b105) that curves along the front edge of the face as the smile.
I assumed the blue plate and the curved tile sit on the new white plate b103. I put the new half-round plate over b47, b54, b55 and b56. These supports are my best reading of the drawing.

Step 33 adds a white 2x3 plate (b106) on top of the gray centre plate b100 (the nose or brow), two black 1x2 tiles (b107, b108) on the ears, and two white 1x1 quarter tiles (b109, b110) on the lower-face plate.
I took the black tiles to be lego-3069b (Tile 1x2 with Groove, Black) from the parts list. I put one on each ear plate, b52 and b53.
The white quarter-tile positions are only roughly visible, so I placed them on b103 as my best guess.

Step 34 is built 2x. Each copy is a white 2x6 round-corner plate with two black half-circle 1x1 tiles that together make an oval pupil. The copies are placed side by side at the eye positions on the face.
The 2x box and the arrows show two identical copies. I listed all 6 pieces (b111-b116).
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing, since the eye plates overlap the hair plate b99, the gray plate b100 and the white 2x3 plate b106.

Step 35 adds a yellow 2x2 round plate with an axle hole (b117, the centre of the face), a light bluish gray hinge brick base (b118) and two black 2x2 curved macaroni tiles (b119, b120). The curved tiles arc around the lower face.
I identified the gray piece as the 1x2 hinge brick base (lego-3937) from its shape. It is probably the base for a hinged top plate later.
The supports in rests_on are my best reading of the drawing.
Step 36 is built 2x. Each copy is a red angled heart plate with two white 1x1 round tiles as polka dots. One copy goes on each ear plate, b52 (left) and b53 (right), beside the bow.
I listed all 6 pieces (b121-b126). I paired each heart with the ear plate it sits on.
Step 37 adds a red 2x2 round tile with a bottom stud holder (b127) in the middle of the bow, between the two red heart plates b121 and b122 on the ears.
I assumed it clutches studs on both hearts. It may also overlap the earlier bow sub-assembly b94 and its tiles.

Step 38 adds a white 2x6 double round-corner plate (b128) on the upper face over the two eye plates, two white 1x1 plates (b129, b130), and two white 1x1 quarter tiles (b131, b132). The tiles are shown dropping onto the new plate's corners.
The remaining-parts list suggests white quarter tiles were already used up, so the quarter tiles here may actually be red. I kept the white seen in the drawing.
Where the two 1x1 plates sit is not clear from the drawing; I put one beside each eye plate. All supports are my best guess.
Step 39 adds two black 1x2 grille tiles (b133, b134), one at the outer edge of each eye plate (b111, b112), as eyelashes.

Correction to page 15: I recorded the two black tiles b48 and b49 there as lego-2412b grille tiles. The parts list has only two grille tiles, so those were probably plain black 1x2 tiles (lego-3069b), and the grille tiles belong here. I can't change b48 and b49 on this page.

Step 40 adds a white 1x2 plate (b135) with a white 1x2 grooved tile pressed on top (b136), and two white 1x2 sloped bricks (b137, b138). Together they make a raised nose on the face, sitting on the hinge brick b118 and the 2x3 plate b106.
Exactly which studs the slopes clutch is my best reading of the drawing.

Step 41 builds Minnie's nose. A black round dome brick (b140) is pressed onto a white 1x2 hinge top plate (b139). The assembly is then clipped onto the gray hinge brick base b118 that sits in the middle of the face.

The small plate icon is not clearly labelled. By elimination from the remaining-parts list, and because it shows a hinge finger on the end, I identified it as the white thin hinge top plate (lego-3938).
The red jumper plate lego-15573 is no longer in the list; it was used earlier as b59. The nose can pivot on the hinge.
This page has no building step. It shows the finished model from the back, with the U-shaped handle swung out on its hinges as a stand.
The yellow and white 1x2 grooved tiles (lego-3069b) still show as unplaced. They may be spares, or the manual may use them on a later page.
This page has no building step. It shows the finished Minnie Mouse model standing up on its folded-out stand.
This page is an advertisement for the LEGO product feedback prize draw, with copyright text. It has no building step, so it adds no pieces.
The yellow and white 1x2 grooved tiles (lego-3069b) were never placed in any step I saw. They are probably spare pieces, though the manual may place them on a page I didn't see.
